1928, March
FR. SOLANUS, NOTEBOOK NO, 1.
Page 40 Cont.
March 2nd Mr. OBrien Enrolled in the Mass - Ass'n on Jan. 28th and enrolled the schemers as well. The property is saved. Now he is offered $90,000.00 for the property - 75 acres. Deo Gratias
Blood Poison Tho's Hughes 50 to have blood-transfusion To-day. Two days will indicate whether the arm must be amputated or not.
March 22
Dying? 7.30 p.m. Charles T. Murphy
Page 41 1929
1929, June
June 1st Mrs. Margaret Mahoney ( 63) of Emerald, Wis, enrolled April 23rd then supposed to be dying - or dead - enlargement of heart, bron- chitis, "Flue" and pneumonia. Her daughter expected to find her dead and found her decidedly improving, now up and around for herself .
June 4th Non-Catholic Ninin MacQuicker 87 of 714 Jos Campo, enrolled by a poor neighbor for one year May 20th as a cancerous paralytic, re- ported To-day as quite improving.
11 Jacob W. Julich (52) 9039 Brydn Ave. - baptized Catholic Confirmed away from church over 30 years. He had given up practice of reli- gion as a German soldier - Experienced in politics - sub-marine expert during war - has patents ... May 11th had serious accident, breaking three ribs etc. His mother who had died when he was a baby 9 months old appeared very vividly holding rosary in her hands she said nothing but her atitude imprest him.
14 Harry B. Mulligan 27 of Seattle, rumatic for three years and now crippled (arthritis) comes To-day and is inscribed in S.M.A.
July 12 Patrick Cabrey 38, 5618 - 14 st Detroit now quite recovered from accident September 19th last year. (1928) Working for a "wrecking Company" was thrown 150 feet in air coming down head-first on pile of brick and slate rubbish. ... Falling chimney had struck scant- ling on which he stood sending him in air .... Bleeding and blind and semi-conscious asked nurse sister in St. Joseph's to phone mon- astery and enroll him in S. Mass Assoc'n, which she did and immedi- ately bleeding stops.
